children.text: Georgian citizens need the appropriate visa category to travel to the US. The visa category depends on the purpose of the trip. For example, if a person is traveling to the US for tourism, they can apply for a B1/B2 category visa; if for studies, an F1 category, and so on. However, business and work visas cause some confusion among travelers, and in many cases are even conflated. Today in this blog, we'll go over what business and work visas mean, what the difference is between them, and how to apply for each.
To obtain a business visa, it's important that the traveler have a scheduled business visit in the US, which includes the following areas:
A short-term trip, the purpose of which should be meetings, participating in exhibitions, or conducting negotiations
A visit to local organizations without compensation (during the visit, the inviting organization should not be paying you a salary)
A letter of invitation, sent to you by the inviting organization

All the areas listed above fall under a temporary business visit, which in turn falls under the B1 visa category. Accordingly, individuals wishing to travel to the US for a business visit must hold a B1 category visa, or the combined B1/B2 category.

page.title: What Does a Business Visa Cover?

children.text: To obtain a US business visa, it's important to fully complete the following steps:
🔹 You pay the visa fee
🔹 You complete the electronic application form (DS-160).
🔹 You schedule your interview date.
🔹 You go through the interview with a consular officer, who makes the final decision regarding the visa.
After successfully completing all the steps, you will receive your US business visa, for which the official waiting period is 4 to 10 business days.

page.title: What Steps Do You Need to Take to Obtain a Business Visa?

children.text: Individuals who wish to work in the US temporarily, under non-immigrant status, must hold a US work visa. For this, it's important for the applicant to submit a letter of invitation received from the employing organization. Accordingly, during a work visit, the traveler receives the appropriate salary and has the right to work and live in the country long-term.

page.title: What Does a Work Visa Cover?

children.text: Just as with a business visa, to obtain a work visa, at the initial stage you must pay the visa fee, complete a special application (DS-160), create a profile, and schedule your interview date.
To create a profile and schedule a date, you'll need the following three pieces of data:
🔹 Your passport number
🔹 Your visa fee payment receipt number
🔹 Your DS-160 application number
After successfully completing all the processes mentioned above, you go through an interview with a consular officer, who will make the final decision regarding the visa.

So, work and business visas are issued for different purposes, though the visa process is similar in both cases. However, with a work visa, the traveler receives the corresponding salary, which doesn't happen during a business visit.
